Hi Olga / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We are getting ready to kick off the private deployment (VPC) next month and need to confirm the full connectivity and access clearance sweep so our networking and security teams can provision resources. High-level asks from our side:

- Required public IP ranges / NAT egress patterns
- Minimum firewall ACLs and ports for control-plane + data-plane (ingress/egress)
- Enclave peering steps and expected CIDR overlap checks
- KMS/HSM integration requirements and key rotation guidance
- IAM/service account permissions your installer will need
- Any support windows / jumpbox access expectations during the handoff

If you can provide a concise preflight checklist and any commands/snippets we can run, we’ll align our infra schedule and come back with our network diagram (we’ll attach it to follow-up). Ideally we’d complete the clearance by 2027-04-22 to hit our deployment date on 04-29.

Appreciate it,
Jordan

Jordan — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a compact preflight sweep (redwood_private_onboard_sweep_v1.1.pdf) that maps our standard requirements to what you listed. I also captured a short runbook of the order we normally validate things in (network -> peering -> secrets -> KMS -> validation). Quick notes inline below: 

- Public egress: Our control-plane callbacks originate from these ranges: 34.214.120.0/22 and 52.12.64.0/24. You'll want NAT egress to allow outbound to these ranges for health checks and metrics. If your security policy requires static egress IPs, we can discuss alternatives.

- Firewall ports: Control-plane: TCP 443 outbound. Data-plane (model traffic): TCP 443 and optional 10000-10100 for GRPC if you plan to use non-HTTP transport for bulk replication.

- Peering: We prefer a dedicated VPC-peering or AWS Transit attachment w/ explicit route table entries. Avoid overlapping /20 CIDRs; we can accept /16-24 ranges but must not overlap existing Redwood peering pools (we flagged common overlaps in the attached checklist).

- KMS: We support customer-managed KMS keys. Provide key ARN + IAM principal for our service account. Key rotation is your responsibility; we recommend a 90-day rotation cadence and will respect Destroy/Disable policies during secret refresh windows.

- IAM: Create an onboarding service account with these IAM permissions: iam.serviceAccounts.actAs, kms:Decrypt (for the key ARN), ec2:CreateNetworkInterface (if you allow peered ENIs), and logs:Write for the logging sink. Exact policy snippets are in page 3 of the attached PDF.

- Support access: We request a temporary bastion/jumpbox with restricted access (SSH key pair or temporary SSM access) for the initial verification window (4 hours). We will not leave persistent access without an approved ticket (Jira ticket preferred).

Next steps: Ben and I will review your network diagram when you send it. Ben — I’ve flagged the peering/CIDR validations for you to comment on.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Sales (Onboarding Lead) — Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Adding a few operational specifics we’ve found helpful during handoffs — putting the tactical bits here so your infra team can copy/paste: 

- VPC peering checks (commands):
  - aws ec2 describe-vpcs --filters "Name=cidr,Values=*" --query 'Vpcs[*].{Id:VpcId,Cidr:CidrBlock}'
  - route table validation: aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters "Name=vpc-id,Values=<your-vpc-id>"

- If using cross-account peering, ensure the peering accepter role has ec2:AcceptVpcPeeringConnection.

- NAT recommendations: Use a small pool of egress NATs for predictable outbound identification; we include the nat ip ranges in the attached peering-commands.txt for reference.

- MTU: Set tunnel MTU to 1412 for IPSec VPNs to avoid fragmentation for model payloads > 1MB.

- Load testing window: We ask for a 30-minute window for an initial smoke load (100 concurrent requests with typical payloads) after peering is in place. This helps validate routing, egress, and caching behavior.

I also attached a short text file with the exact peering and iptables snippets we run during verification.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
Attachment: peering-commands.txt (text)
